verses.verse:
न्यासापन्यास विन्यास सन्यासास्तु विरामकाः।
न्यूनाधिकम् महत्वं तु स्वराणां यैस्तु संभवः।११८।
verses.text: Nyāsa, apanyāsa, vinyāsa and sanyāsa are the pauses, through which the greater or lesser importance of the notes comes about.

commentary.text: On the notes of greater or lesser importance in rāgas we use four kinds of pause. First, we play many note groups ending on the vādī (principal) note, one after another, and in each of those note groups we make an ordinary pause; this we call nyāsa (resting note). The slight short pause that we make on some other note in order to complete that nyāsa, we call upanyāsa. If within the nyāsa we utter a particular note group again and again and reinforce it in many ways, we call these pauses vinyāsa (varied rest), because variety and distinctiveness are both expressed by the prefix 'vi'. And when, after these nyāsas, we come to Sa and feel rest, this is called sanyāsa (final rest on Sa). For example, in Rāga Yaman, on the note Gāndhāra: Ni Re Ga, PaMa′ Ga, Re Ma′ Ga - these are nyāsas. And NiRe Ga ReGa Ma′ PaMa′ Ga, Ṇi Ḍha Ṇi Re Ma′ Ga, Ṇi Ṇi Re - Ṇi Ṇi Ga - - these are all vinyāsas endowed with the qualities of alaṅkāra; and ṆiRe GaMa′ Pa -- PaMa′ Ga: here, after making apanyāsa on Pañcama, the nyāsa of Ga took place. Then Ga Re -- ṆiRe Sa. Here, after making apanyāsa on Re, sanyāsa was made on Sa.
